independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently: psalm_device_inventory.json confirms Ps 78's superscription carries both the maskil and le_asaph labels, and web_mt_offset_map.json confirms Ps 78 is an identity psalm (web_title true, mt_title_verses empty -- the title sits inside MT v1), matching the row's numbering claim exactly. citation_sweep.py's Hebrew-quote-binding arm returned GREEN over the full cluster, confirming the row's pointed Hebrew (the superscription and the opening imperative) collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.78.1. Reading Ps.78.1-8 against the WEB clean text confirms an unbroken purpose-clause chain (v5's covenant-commission extended by the two 'that ... might' clauses of v6-v7) resolving in the negative exemplar of v8; v9 then supplies a concrete named subject (the children of Ephraim) for the general 'their fathers' of v8 -- a genuine tier-1 subject-specification shift with no comparable seam inside vv1-8. rejected_alternative (a break after v4) is correctly dismissed since v5-v7 continue one purpose-clause sentence. No defect found.

The Ephraim-naming claim re-derives exactly: a skeleton sweep of Ephraim's name (sweep.py --skel) returns 5 verses book-wide, exactly 2 of them in Ps 78 (MT 78:9 and 78:67) -- matching the row's 'exactly 2 verses of this psalm, bracketing the composition' to the digit. Following the boundary_evidence_refs pointer to 78:65-72 (check_refs_mirror.py returns GREEN, confirming the mirroring), the WEB text at web:Ps.78.67 reads “Moreover he rejected the tent of Joseph, and didn’t choose the tribe of Ephraim,” -- the device_notes' bracketing claim holds. The three-verse indictment (covenant broken, law refused, deeds forgotten) is register-distinct from both the general paraenesis of vv1-8 and the itemized recital opening at v12, and medium confidence fairly reflects that this is a genuinely debatable three-verse unit rather than a settled one. rejected_alternative correctly tests and dismisses folding these verses into the recital that follows. No defect found.

The span is sound and among the clearest seams in the psalm: vv12-16 run one uninterrupted wonder-catalogue with no adversative, breaking cleanly against the adverb opening v17 -- a skeleton sweep (sweep.py --skel) of that adverb returns exactly 3 verses in Ps 78 (78:17, 78:30, 78:32), confirming v17's opening particle is genuinely distinctive against vv12-16. The Zoan-inclusio count also re-derives exactly: a skeleton sweep returns 2 verses book-wide total, both inside this psalm (78:12, 78:43), matching the row's count precisely. One evidence-discipline defect: check_universals.py flags the rationale's absence claim as an unswept universal-class assertion with no adjacent digit-bearing citation. See challenge LF-239-1.

challenges.claim: The rationale's absence claim 'with no note of complaint or unbelief' (describing vv78.12-16) is an unswept universal-class assertion with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation, contrary to the book's count-object discipline for universal claims.
challenges.evidence: check_universals.py flags this exact span: path [2].rationale, matched claim 'with no note of complaint or unbelief', context '...and water from the rock (web:Ps.78.15-web:Ps.78.16) — with no note of complaint or unbelief. The tone breaks sharply at web:Ps.78.17...' -- no sweep count of the form 'N verses'/'N occurrences' appears within the required window on either side.

reviews.reasoning: The core seam is solid: v17's adverb opens the sin-cycle against the wonder-catalogue that precedes it, and the causal chain from the food-testing taunt (vv18-20) through Yahweh's anger (v21) to its explicit cause (v22) closes cleanly before v23's fresh divine initiative. The tempting-verb recurrence count re-derives exactly: a skeleton sweep (sweep.py --skel) returns 4 verses book-wide (78:18, 78:41, 78:56, 106:14), 3 of them inside Ps 78 as claimed. One terminology defect: the device_notes calls the fourth occurrence (Ps 106:14) 'a typed cross-psalm relation ... never a merge' -- but no such relation is registered anywhere in psalm_device_inventory.json or the book strategy's typed-relation roster. See challenge LF-240-1.

challenges.claim: The device_notes labels the shared tempting-verb wording with Ps 106:14 'a typed cross-psalm relation' -- campaign-specific terminology reserved for the ratified doublet/refrain/acrostic-pair roster -- when no such registered relation between Ps 78 and Ps 106 exists in psalm_device_inventory.json or the book strategy.
challenges.evidence: sweep.py --skel on the tempting-verb form returns 4 verses book-wide: Ps.78.18, Ps.78.41, Ps.78.56, Ps.106.14 (skeleton count). psalm_device_inventory.json has no relations/doublets registry entry naming Ps 106, and Ps.md's typed-relation roster (14=53, 40:13-17=70, 57+60=108, the 9-10 acrostic pair, the 42-43 refrain pair) does not include Ps 78 or Ps 106 -- the shared wording is a bare lexical echo, not a typed relation.

reviews.reasoning: The row keeps vv23-31 as one strophe on the grammatical-dependency argument that v30's craving clause depends on the meal narrated in vv24-29. But the row's own device evidence undercuts this: the same adverb it identifies as opening v17 (row M8-Ps-240's strophe) and v32 (row M8-Ps-242's strophe, whose own device_notes calls it the marker that 'marks the opening of every sin-turn in this cycle-pair') also opens v30 -- a skeleton sweep confirms exactly 3 hits in Ps 78 (78:17, 78:30, 78:32), no more, no fewer. The marker is honored as a strophe-opening signal at two of its three occurrences (78:17, 78:32) but not the third (78:30), which stays buried mid-span. The rejected_alternative addresses only clause-dependency and never engages the marker's own established pattern, leaving a real rival seam at 78:29|78:30 undisclosed. See challenge LF-241-1.

challenges.claim: A rival seam at Ps.78.29|Ps.78.30 has better tier-1 warrant than the row discloses: the adverb the row's own cluster treats as the psalm's recurring sin-cycle opener (at 78:17 and 78:32) also opens 78:30, and the row's rejected_alternative never addresses that pattern before dismissing the split.
challenges.evidence: sweep.py --skel on the adverb returns exactly 3 verses in Ps 78: Ps.78.17, Ps.78.30, Ps.78.32 (skeleton count, no others in-psalm). Row M8-Ps-240 treats this adverb as opening its own strophe at 78:17 ('opens the unit on the adverb ... absent from web:Ps.78.12-web:Ps.78.16'); the sibling row's device_notes for 78:32 calls it the marker that 'marks the opening of every sin-turn in this cycle-pair' across all three of its occurrences, including 78:30 -- yet this row's own span (78:23-31) does not treat 78:30 as an opening boundary, and its rejected_alternative argues only from clause grammar, not from the marker pattern the cluster elsewhere relies on.

reviews.reasoning: vv32-39 read as one coherent sin/consequence/repentance/mercy arc: v32's adverb opens against the previous cycle (confirmed as the third of exactly 3 in-psalm hits, skeleton sweep), v33 draws the consequence, vv34-37 narrate a repentance the psalm itself marks insincere, and vv38-39 resolve on Yahweh's restraint. v40's exclamation reopens in a quantifying register distinct from the narrated-mercy close of v38-39, supporting the row's seam. Unlike the sibling row at 78:23-31, this row's own use of the adverb as its strophe-opening signal is internally consistent with how the marker is used at 78:17 -- no comparable rival-seam problem here. rejected_alternative correctly tests and dismisses merging forward into vv40-42 on the resolution/reopening register contrast. No defect found.

The span itself is honestly calibrated: the row discloses its own rear-seam uncertainty explicitly, consistent with v42's relative clause grammatically continuing into v43 even though the recital genre changes there -- an appropriate medium-confidence, non-overclaiming register. The interrogative-particle sweep re-derives exactly: sweep.py --skel returns 9 verses book-wide, one of them Ps.78.40, matching '1 verse in this psalm, 9 verses book-wide' precisely. One quote-convention defect: check_web_quotes.py flags observed_substrate_signals[0] -- the curly-quoted English gloss 'how often/how much' sits beside only an oshb: ref with no web: ref anywhere in the same field, and the phrase is not itself a verbatim WEB quotation. See challenge LF-243-1.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[0] presents the English gloss 'how often/how much' in curly quotes with no web: ref in its field, violating the mandatory curly-quote-plus-inline-web:-ref convention and reading as a paraphrase presented as a WEB quotation.
challenges.evidence: check_web_quotes.py flags: path [6].observed_substrate_signals[0], quote text 'how often/how much', refs_nearby: [], issue 'curly quote with NO web: ref in its field'. The field's only ref is oshb:Ps.78.40; TOOLKIT.md states curly quotes plus an inline web: ref in the same field are mandatory at every layer, and the actual WEB text at web:Ps.78.40 reads “How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness, and grieved him in the desert!” -- a gloss of the Hebrew interrogative, not that verbatim string.

reviews.reasoning: The span's boundaries are sound: v43's field-name notice explicitly reopens the geographic notice of v12 (skeleton sweep confirms exactly 2 verses book-wide, both here), launching a plague catalogue that runs one grammatical chain through v51's firstborn climax; web:Ps.78.52 (“But he led out his own people like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.”) is a clean topic shift from Egypt's affliction to Israel's departure, confirmed by direct reading of the WEB text. rejected_alternative correctly tests and dismisses a split at 47|48 on the ground that only the plague type changes there -- but that observation is in tension with the main rationale, which mislabels the plague grouping. See challenge LF-244-1.

challenges.claim: The rationale groups vv78.46-47 together as 'locust-plagues,' but v47's content (hail and frost destroying vines and sycamore fig trees) is a hail plague, not a locust plague -- only v46 (caterpillar/locust on crops) is locust content.
challenges.evidence: Hebrew (oshb:Ps.78.46, byte tier): “וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לֶחָסִ֣יל יְבוּלָ֑ם וִֽ֝יגִיעָ֗ם לָאַרְבֶּֽה” -- caterpillar/locust vocabulary (WEB: “He also gave their increase to the caterpillar, and their labor to the locust.”). Hebrew (oshb:Ps.78.47, byte tier): “יַהֲרֹ֣ג בַּבָּרָ֣ד גַּפְנָ֑ם וְ֝שִׁקְמוֹתָ֗ם בַּֽחֲנָמַֽל” -- hail/frost vocabulary (WEB: “He destroyed their vines with hail, their sycamore fig trees with frost.”). The hail root recurs verbatim at oshb:Ps.78.48 (byte tier): “וַיַּסְגֵּ֣ר לַבָּרָ֣ד בְּעִירָ֑ם וּ֝מִקְנֵיהֶ֗ם לָרְשָׁפִֽים” (WEB: “He also gave over their livestock to the hail, and their flocks to hot thunderbolts.”), tying v47's content to the hail plague of v48 rather than v46's locust vocabulary. The row's own rejected_alternative implicitly concedes the plague type changes at 47|48, in tension with the main rationale's grouping 'locust-plagues (web:Ps.78.46-web:Ps.78.47)'.
